conventions.convention: Continuous-kernel Nyström operators act on the real Banach space C([0,1], R) with the supremum norm; continuous integrands use ordinary Riemann integration.
Composite midpoint sampling uses N ≥ 1, h = 1/N, nodes (j + 1/2)h for 0 ≤ j < N, and weights h.

Collective compactness means compact closure of the union of all closed-unit-ball images. Consistency means norm convergence on each fixed input, without asserting operator-norm convergence. The stability theorem assumes AC and a nonzero Banach space.
The half-order integral is the limit of Riemann integrals excluding (x − ε, x + ε); empty intervals contribute zero. Its positive functional has norm 2√x + 2√(1 − x) ≤ 2√2.
Product integration uses endpoint-inclusive nodes j/n for 0 ≤ j ≤ n and piecewise-linear hats, interpolating a(x,y)u(y) while integrating the singular factor exactly.
The midpoint rate assumes a uniform second-derivative bound for the actual integrand k(x,y)u(y), rather than smoothness of arbitrary continuous inputs.
The product-integration rate requires each a(x,·)u(·) to extend to a C² function on a neighborhood of [0,1], with a uniform second-derivative bound.
The Gaussian example assumes Countable Choice when identifying continuous Riemann integrals with Lebesgue integrals.

load_bearing.statement: Assume AC. On a nonzero Banach space, let K be compact and K_n bounded linear, with compact closure of the union of their closed-unit-ball images and K_n x → Kx for every x. If I−K is injective, then I−K_n is eventually boundedly invertible with a uniform inverse bound C, and solution errors satisfy ||u_n−u|| ≤ C(||(K_n−K)u|| + ||f_n−f||).

For Fu = Σ_j ψ_j u(y_j) with continuous ψ_j and M_ij = δ_ij − ψ_j(y_i), solutions of (I−F)u=f correspond bijectively to solutions of Mc=b through u=f+Σ_j ψ_j c_j and c_i=u(y_i). The nullspaces are linearly isomorphic; I−F is bijective if and only if M is nonsingular.

Assume AC and continuous a on [0,1]². The half-order operators K and K_n are bounded linear maps on C([0,1], R); K is compact, and K_n are collectively compact and converge pointwise in norm to K. Their nonnegative weights sum to 2√x + 2√(1−x) ≤ 2√2. Under the stated C² extension and uniform derivative hypothesis, ||K_nu−Ku||∞ ≤ (√2/4)M₂h².
Assume AC and a continuous kernel on [0,1]². Composite midpoint Nyström operators are bounded linear, collectively compact, and satisfy ||K_Nu−Ku||∞ → 0 for every u in C([0,1], R); K is compact.
For x in [0,1] and continuous real g, the cutoff improper integral S_x(g) exists. S_x is linear and positive with ||S_x|| = S_x(1) = 2√x + 2√(1−x) ≤ 2√2.
The improper integrals T(x,x′) = ∫₀¹ ||x−y|^(−1/2) − |x′−y|^(−1/2)| dy exist, with T(x,x)=0; their supremum over |x−x′| ≤ d is finite and tends to zero as d decreases to zero.

seams_checked.note: The actual citing item is thm-volume-product-integration-solution-and-far-field-error, F3 and steps 1.1–3.1. It faithfully states the generic collective-compactness theorem, retains AC and the nonzero Banach-space hypothesis, and separately verifies boundedness, pointwise convergence, collective compactness, compactness of K, and injectivity of I−K on complex L²(D). The supplier is formulated on a general Banach space, so this use does not extend the real continuous-kernel specialization. The assigned pages contain no reverse logical citation to the scattering page.
